column1: # Mutation tests for the foundation self-test — see scripts/analysis/check-mutations.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A check that is broken and a check that is passing both return
# zero rows. That is the only signal SQL gives, so "it returned nothing on healthy data"
# is not evidence a check works — it is exactly what a no-op does. Every defect found in
# this suite so far was a check that had silently become a no-op, usually because a
# comparison went NULL. This file breaks the catalog on purpose, one way per line, and
# asserts the check that is supposed to notice actually does.
#   name            what is being broken, for the report
#   expect          check_name that MUST appear. `*` means "any row at all" — avoid it:
#                   it passes when the WRONG check fires, so it proves almost nothing
#   sql             statements redefining a view/macro to introduce the defect
# Adding a check to catalog_checks.sql? Add a line here breaking what it guards. A check
# with no line is a check nobody has proven fires — and the harness ENFORCES that, in
# both directions: a check with no mutation fails the run, and an entry naming a check
# that no longer exists fails it too.
